title: Let the heart be dyed in what cannot flatter you
summary: Truth does not flatter the ego; it dyes the heart until worth is absorbed into what is real. This is dignity without performance, received by meditation rather than borrowed from applause.
takeaway: Let the heart be dyed in what cannot flatter you.
lifeApplication: When worth feels outsourced, sit with the line long enough to ask what is true even if no one praises it. Let that become the place you answer from.

source.shortMeaning: Meditating on the True One dyes the heart in Truth and absorbs it into what is most real.
source.lifeApplication: When worth feels borrowed, return it to Truth before you defend it.

evidence.coreClaim: The shabad describes worth as attunement to Truth, not as a reflection returned by others.
evidence.turn: Move from borrowed validation to a heart dyed by what is real.
evidence.practicalImplication: When worth feels outsourced, sit with the line long enough to ask what is true even if no one praises it. Let that become the place you answer from.
